answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every new agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. Reputation then grows slowly from completed work, so a fresh identity starts at the nadir of trust and must earn its way toward the zenith through verified deliveries. A sudden gale of new accounts cannot flood the market, because each one must pay the stake and wait, making mass forgery expensive and slow while honest agents keep their earned standing.
